justifications.layering: Data flows cleanly from sources (`_ergast__sources.yml`) through 1:1 staging models with shared macros (`macros/ergast_casts.sql`) to intermediates (`int_season_calendar_progress`, `int_pit_stops_enriched`) and marts, all via ref/source, and `mart_driver_season_standings` is derived from `mart_driver_standings_by_round` instead of re-implemented; however `fct_session_results.sql` repeats the races/constructors/status joins and the `is_win`/`is_podium` logic from `fct_results.sql` rather than one being built on the other.
justifications.naming: Naming is consistent throughout: `stg_ergast__*`, `base_ergast__drivers`, `int_*`, `fct_`/`dim_`/`mart_` prefixes, `assert_*` singular tests, one `_<dir>__models.yml` / `_<dir>__unit_tests.yml` per folder, and snake_case columns with unit suffixes (`duration_ms`, `fastest_lap_time_ms`, `altitude_m`); a new teammate could find things easily.
justifications.testing: Tests sit at the right layers: source drift tests plus warn-level source uniqueness (`tests/generic/source_schema_drift.sql`), error-level key and grain tests in staging, and business-rule reconciliations in the marts (`assert_world_champions_match_official_record` against a seed, `assert_modern_standings_reconcile_with_race_points`, `assert_one_winner_per_sprint`); the ticket 5 rename is caught by `declared_columns_exist` and the ticket 6 Ferrari fan-out by `assert_fct_results_has_no_join_fanout` and `assert_pit_stop_mart_accounts_for_every_stop`. Small gap: no not_null tests on the `stg_ergast__lap_times` keys.
justifications.quirks: Every listed quirk is handled on purpose and documented: `\N` and empty strings in `ergast_clean`; mixed lap-time formats in `lap_time_to_ms` (with a unit test); red-flag stops via the `max_pit_stop_seconds` var in `int_pit_stops_enriched`; sprints kept separate in `fct_session_results` and in `career_sprint_wins`; pre-1991 dropped scores and the 1997 exclusion taken from official standings; shared drives counted with `count(distinct race_id)` in `dim_drivers_v2`; the incomplete 2024 season gated by `int_season_calendar_progress`; the `TRY_TO_NUMBER('E')` trap; the Colapinto nationality fix; and late-arriving drivers left-joined in `dim_drivers_v2`. All are in the README 'Data quirks found' list. The one inconsistency is that sprint `finish_position` doesn't get the same positionText fallback as GP results.
justifications.incremental_snapshot: `fct_lap_times.sql` uses delete+insert on `race_id`, a configurable lookback ordered by (season, round) because race_id isn't chronological, and documents full-refresh for older corrections; `snp_drivers.yml` rightly uses `check` on all columns with `hard_deletes: invalidate` over a deduplicated base model. But the filter is purely `>= reprocess_from`, so a race that arrives late with an earlier (season, round) than the window is never loaded, despite the header promising 'races not yet loaded'; and snapshotting raw untrimmed text means whitespace-only vendor changes create new versions.
justifications.change_hygiene: Later tickets refactored rather than bolted on: ticket 3 deleted `int_driver_season_final_standings` and rebuilt season standings from by-round standings; ticket 5 changed only staging and the sources YAML; ticket 6 fixed the root cause across all staging models and added guards; ticket 7 made v1 a thin layer over v2. There's no commented-out or dead code. Small leftovers: the misaligned `as position_order` lines in `stg_ergast__results.sql` and `stg_ergast__sprint_results.sql`, and the `select distinct` comment block repeated in all 14 staging files.
justifications.docs: The README and model headers explain the *why* well: why standings aren't recomputed (dropped scores and the 1997 exclusion), why the season-complete test is meant to fail until a person adds the champion seed, why the lookback is ordered by (season, round), and write-ups for the Ferrari incident and the vendor migration. Mart columns in `_core__models.yml` are well described, though most staging columns have no descriptions.
justifications.interfaces: `fct_results` and `dim_drivers` are public with enforced contracts and explicit casts. `dim_drivers` is versioned: v1 has a `deprecation_date`, keeps its original relation through an alias, and keeps its column order through an explicit YAML-anchor column list; it is built from v2 so the two can't drift, and the README has a migration guide. Unit tests use realistic edge cases: an in-progress season leader, a null-position exclusion, sub-minute and whitespace lap times.

biggest_strength: Defensive vendor-data engineering backed by tests: source schema-drift tests (`tests/generic/source_schema_drift.sql`), deduplication on cleaned values in staging plus error-level unique tests, and reconciliation tests against independent references (the `official_world_champions` seed and staging row and point totals). Together these catch exactly the ticket 5 rename and the ticket 6 Ferrari fan-out, and every rule is documented with its reason.
biggest_weakness: Leadership's analytical questions ('overperform their car', 'are pit stops getting faster') were never answered: there's no teammate-relative or car-adjusted model and no trend analysis, only the descriptive `mart_constructor_season_pit_stops`. Separately, the `fct_lap_times` lookback silently skips a late-arriving race older than the reprocess window, and `fct_session_results` duplicates `fct_results`' join and flag logic.
